{{Short description|Conjecture in modular representation theory}}

The '''Brauer Height Zero Conjecture''' is a [[conjecture]] in [[modular representation theory]] of [[finite group]]s relating the degrees of the [[complex number|complex]] irreducible [[character theory|characters]] in a [[Modular representation theory|Brauer block]] and the structure of its [[Modular representation theory#Defect groups|defect groups]]. It was formulated by [[Richard Brauer]] in 1955. The proof was completed in 2024.

==Statement==
Let <math>G</math> be a finite group and <math>p</math> a [[prime number|prime]]. The set <math>{\rm Irr}(G)</math> of irreducible complex [[Character theory|characters]] can be partitioned into Brauer <math>p</math>-[[Modular representation theory#Blocks_and_the_structure_of_the_group_algebra|blocks]]. To each <math>p</math>-block <math>B</math> is canonically associated a conjugacy class of [[p-group|<math>p</math>-subgroups]] of <math>G</math>, called the [[Modular representation theory#Defect groups|defect groups]] of <math>B</math>. The set of irreducible characters belonging to <math>B</math> is denoted by <math>\mathrm{Irr}(B)</math>.

Let <math>\nu</math> be the [[discrete valuation]] defined on the [[integer]]s by <math>\nu(mp^a)=a</math> where <math>m</math> is coprime to <math>p</math>. Brauer proved that if <math>B</math> is a block with defect group <math>D</math> then <math>\nu(\chi(1))\geq \nu(|G:D|)</math> for each <math>\chi\in\mathrm{Irr}(B)</math>. The ''height'' of <math>\chi</math> is defined to be the non-negative integer ''<math>h:=\nu(\chi(1))-\nu(|G:D|)</math>'' .

'''Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture''' asserts that <math>\nu(\chi(1))=\nu(|G:D|)</math> for all <math>\chi\in\mathrm{Irr}(B)</math> if and only if <math>D</math> is [[abelian group|abelian]]. In other words: all irreducible complex characters belonging to a block have height zero if and only if the block's defect group is abelian. 

==History==

Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture was formulated by [[Richard Brauer]] in 1955.<ref> {{cite book| last1 = Brauer | first1 = Richard D. | year = 1956 | title = Proceedings of the International Symposium on Algebraic Number Theory, Tokyo and Nikko, 1955 | chapter = Number theoretical investigations on groups of finite order | publisher=Science Council of Japan| pages=55–62}}</ref> It also appeared as Problem 23 in Brauer's list of problems.<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Brauer | first1 = Richard D. | year = 1963 | chapter =  Representations of finite groups|title= Lectures on Modern Mathematics
| volume=1 | publisher=  Wiley | pages=133–175 }}</ref> Brauer's Problem 12 of the same list asks whether the [[character table]] of a finite group <math>G</math> determines if its Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroups are abelian. Solving Brauer's height zero conjecture for blocks whose defect groups are Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroups (or equivalently, that contain a character of degree coprime to <math>p</math>) also gives a solution to Brauer's Problem 12.

=== Proof ===
The proof of the ''if'' direction of the conjecture was completed by [[Radha Kessar]] and [[Gunter Malle]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kessar|first1=Radha|last2=Malle|first2=Gunter|title=Quasi-isolated blocks and Brauer's height zero conjecture|doi=10.4007/annals.2013.178.1.6 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=178 |date=2013|pages=321–384|arxiv=1112.2642}}</ref> in 2013 after a reduction to [[finite simple group]]s by Thomas R. Berger and Reinhard Knörr.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Berger | first1=Thomas R. | last2=Knörr | first2=Reinhard | title=On Brauer's height 0 conjecture | journal=[[Nagoya Mathematical Journal]] | volume=109 | date=1988 | pages=109–116 | doi=10.1017/S0027763000002798 }}
</ref>

The ''only if'' direction was proved for [[Solvable group#p-solvable|<math>p</math>-solvable]] groups by David Gluck and Thomas R. Wolf in 1984.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Gluck|first1=David|last2=Wolf|first2=Thomas R.|title=Brauer's height conjecture for p-solvable groups
|journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=282|date=1984|issue=1 |pages=137–152|doi=10.2307/1999582
|jstor=1999582 }}</ref> The so-called generalized Gluck—Wolf theorem, which was a main obstacle towards a proof of the Height Zero Conjecture was proven by [[Gabriel Navarro Ortega|Gabriel Navarro]] and [[Pham Huu Tiep]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Navarro | first1 = Gabriel | last2 = Tiep | first2 = Pham Huu | title = Characters of relative <math>p'</math>-degree over normal subgroups | journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]] | volume = 178 | year = 2013 | pages = 1135–1171 | doi = 10.4007/annals.2013.178 | doi-broken-date = 18 August 2025 }}</ref> Gabriel Navarro and Britta Späth showed in 2014 that the so-called '''inductive Alperin—McKay condition''' for simple groups implied Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Navarro|first1=Gabriel| last2=Späth|first2=Britta|
title=On Brauer's height zero conjecture|
journal=[[Journal of the European Mathematical Society]]|volume=16|date=2014|issue=4 |pages=695–747|doi=10.4171/JEMS/444|arxiv=2209.04736}}</ref> Lucas Ruhstorfer completed the proof of these conditions for the case <math>p=2</math> in 2022.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Ruhstorfer|first=Lucas|date=2022|title=The Alperin-McKay conjecture for the prime 2|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]| volume = 201 |issue=2 | pages = 379–457 | arxiv = 2204.06373}}</ref> The case of odd primes was finally settled by Gunter Malle, Gabriel Navarro, A. A. Schaeffer Fry and Pham Huu Tiep in 2024 using a different reduction theorem.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Malle, Gunter|author2=Navarro, Gabriel|author3= Schaeffer Fry, A. A.|author4=Tiep, Pham Huu|title=Brauer's Height Zero Conjecture|year=2024|doi=10.4007/annals.2024.200.2.4  |volume=200 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |issue=2 |pages=557–608|arxiv=2209.04736}}</ref>
